g.text: Extended Data | The reach-latency association is specification-sensitive

text.style: font-size: 8.8px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #536174

g.text: All points are complete outer-held-out trials from one mouse-day; this post-hoc audit tests robustness, not biological generality.

text.style: font-size: 6.6px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #657286

g.text: Interpretation boundary: the augmented ±250-ms analysis yields a positive within-session association, but the estimate weakens under a narrower ±125-ms window and changes with covariate/QC choices. The relation is post hoc and

concentrated partly in M1↔M2 mappings. It may reflect sustained reach-specific organization or event-spacing/window composition. It does not establish behavioral benefit, information flow or causality; independent animals, a locked
window and pre-grasp-only analyses are required.
